research.topic: First X-ray image: Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen, professor of physics at the University of Würzburg (Bavaria, Germany), discovered X-rays on 8 November 1895 while experimenting with cathode-ray tubes. On 22 December 1895 he made the first X-ray photograph of a human body part, his wife Anna Bertha Ludwig's hand, showing her bones and wedding ring; she is reported to have said 'I have seen my death'. Exposure times for such plates were about 15 minutes. His paper 'On a New Kind of Rays' appeared on 28 December 1895; by early 1896 X-rays were in medical use in Europe and America (locating bullets, fractures). Röntgen refused to patent the discovery and received the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901.

myths.myth: X-rays were an American invention — Edison's.
myths.reality: Edison built an early fluoroscope in 1896, but the rays were discovered and first photographed in Würzburg, Germany, by Röntgen in 1895.
